messages:
Priya: Quick sync re: precision profile canary heuristics. After the RFC, ops asked for a clearer failure model for fp8/int8/4bit. I sketched a few ideas, want feedback: short, concrete please.

Mark: High-level: prefer layered safety: 1) micro-canary perf checks (latency/throughput), 2) semantic checks (deg_score/per-task metric), 3) continuity checks (no sudden KL-like spike). Only promote when all pass for X window.

Elena: Agreed. For semantic checks, we need lightweight golden prompts. But long-context customers differ. Proposal: each profile ships two golden sets: short (<=512 tokens) and long (>=2048). Canary evaluates both.

Theo: Implementation caveat: we must avoid expensive evals in the hot path. Run canary in parallel to production traffic sampling (eg 0.5% mirrored) and run async scoring. If scoring fails the async canary, we revert routing gradually.

Priya: Mirroring helps. Also propose a small hysteresis on deg_score: require 3 consecutive 1m windows over threshold before triggering fallback. Avoid flapping. :+1:

Mark: For rollback vs fallback: define rollback = revert model version globally, fallback = route to compatible safer variant for affected requests. Fallback first is safer. Also: for multi-tenant hosts, allow per-tenant override to pin to a profile.

Elena: Edge-case: KV cache incompatibility between quant variants. Two choices: require identical KV serialization or allow fallback with KV reset. Ask infra: what's the cost of resets?

Theo: KV resets cost cold-start latency ~120-200ms on recent runtime; acceptable for interactive but not for low-latency 50ms SLOs. So for low-latency endpoints, we should only allow variants with compatible KV flags. Add a profile field `kv_compatible_with: ["fp8-v1","int8-safe"]`.

Priya: Good. Also add `context_limits` in profile: e.g. `max_fp8_context=2048` and `per_layer_disable=["attn.34","ffn.12"]` to disable fp8 on problematic layers. Where to store? In profile JSON pushed to control plane.

Mark: Calibration: we need an automated cal job that runs sweep over temperature/seeding/beam and produces a quality vs token-cost curve per endpoint. Store the curve as small quantiles in profile metadata so runtime can make tradeoffs.

Elena: UX for Dedicated/Private: customers want explicit accept step. Suggest a CLI `redwood profile apply --file fp8-delta.json --dry-run` which runs local eval and prints pass/fail and a small expected quality delta summary. Private agent exposes a `/v1/profile/check` endpoint.

Theo: For hosted, automation can auto-promote after canary window. For private, default to manual promote unless tenant sets `auto_promote=true`. Document the gRPC check endpoint shape: `{profile_id, sample_prompts_bucket, timeout_ms}`. Keep it tiny.

deploy-bot: Canary job queued: https://ci.internal/runs/98231 — golden-set long/short configured.

Priya: Action items: Theo to draft minimal gRPC/check API and KV compatibility flag, Mark to spec the calibration output schema and hysteresis rule, Elena to author sample golden prompt sets and CI integration steps. We'll reconvene after PRs land. Thanks.
